inspection_outcome: Five Major proof defects and three Minor local errors established; main density theorems not disproved.

findings.location: PDF p.15, Lemma 5.5, proof, and invocation in (5.17)
findings.claim: Nonzero discriminant alone implies a finite uniform count of all |F(X,Y)|<=m.
findings.decisive_evidence: F=X^4-6X^2Y^2+16XY^3-11Y^4=(X-Y)(X^3+X^2Y-5XY^2+11Y^3); F(t,t)=0 for all integer t. I=-8,J=-4, normalized discriminant -944. Thunder Theorem 2 requires finite type on rational subspaces.
findings.impact: False auxiliary count invoked in the central small-gcd estimate and density proofs. No counterexample to the density conclusion is claimed.
findings.repair_limit: The application has nonzero values and primitive vectors; an appropriate uniform replacement including reducible image quartics is needed. Simply assuming finite type discards allowed inputs.

independent_verification.original_claim: Lemma 5.5 bounds all integer pairs with |F|<=m assuming only nonzero discriminant.
evidence_locations: Main pp.11-13 construction; pp.15-16 Lemma 5.5 and (5.17)
Thunder pp.1-3, Theorem 2 on printed p.769
independent_verification.assumptions: A=2,B=1,D=M=1,P=(1,2),k=0. Curve nonsingular, D square-free, M|D, gcd(M,2x)=1, congruence modulo one valid, y!=0.
independent_verification.independent_proof: The actual construction yields F=X^4-6X^2Y^2+16XY^3-11Y^4=(X-Y)(X^3+X^2Y-5XY^2+11Y^3). Exact computation gives I=-8,J=-4, normalized discriminant -944 and ordinary discriminant -241664. Every (t,t), t integral, has F=0. Thus the count is infinite for every m>=1. Thunder requires finite type on every rational subspace; the line X=Y violates it.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The application has primitive vectors and nonzero F(alpha,beta)=M; the zero-line example does not refute a suitably restricted replacement or the principal density conclusion.
independent_verification.impact: False central auxiliary count used in (5.17), Lemma 5.6 and small-gcd density estimates.
independent_verification.repair: Provide a uniform nonzero-value/primitive-pair estimate including the reducible quartics in the actual image.
independent_verification.repair_limits: Simply imposing finite type excludes a legitimate image form. No adequate uniform replacement was proved.

findings.location: PDF p.9, Lemma 3.5, first mean bound and final h1,h2 summation
findings.claim: The proof uses sum_{U<=|u|<2U}f(|u|)<<U for every separable cubic and obtains exponent max(lambda,2).
findings.decisive_evidence: For all odd prime powers f(p^v)=3; f(n)=3^omega(n) on odd integers. Lemma 3.2/Euler-product mean gives summatory order T(log T)^2, contradicting a uniform O(U) dyadic estimate after summation. The 1/h1 factor also has a harmonic sum.
findings.impact: Theorem 1.4 upper proof does not establish its stated logarithmic exponent; the same count enters Lemma 5.6.
findings.repair_limit: Retaining all elementary logarithms gives B(log(2B))^(2lambda). Subsequent exponents become 3,6,7 for lambda=1,2,3. Full-torsion cutoff 15 can compensate for 7 in the main density strategy, conditional on repairing other inputs; original sharper auxiliary statement remains unproved.

independent_verification.original_claim: Lemma 3.5 claims sum_{U<=|u|<2U}f(|u|)<<U for every allowed cubic, then loses a harmonic factor.
independent_verification.assumptions: Fixed C=X(X-Y)(X+Y) is separable, C(1,0)=1, discriminant 4, lambda=3.
independent_verification.independent_proof: For every odd prime p, 0,+1,-1 are distinct simple roots, so Hensel gives f(p^v)=3 for all v and f(n)=3^omega(n) for odd n. The source mean-value relation gives order T(log T)^2. Independently, 3^omega(n)>=2omega(n); summing over odd n<=T and odd p<=sqrt(T) gives at least T sum_p(1/p)-O(pi(sqrt(T))), not O(T). An O(U) bound on all dyadic intervals would imply O(T), contradiction. The subsequent first term has 1/h1 and its sum costs a harmonic logarithm.
independent_verification.counterevidence: This refutes the written estimate, not the sharper final counting theorem itself. For lambda=1 the first omitted factor is one.
independent_verification.impact: Theorem 1.4's stated upper exponent is not proved by this argument; the same bound enters Lemma 5.6.
independent_verification.repair: Keep all logarithms: conservative B(log(2B))^(2lambda), with first exponent (lambda-1)+1+lambda and second lambda+1. Subsequent small-gcd exponents are 3,6,7 including r=0 exceptions. Full-torsion cutoff 15 gives 7-15/2=-1/2.
independent_verification.repair_limits: Conditional on other counting inputs. This does not restore the sharper auxiliary theorem, the original exponent 6, or repair P1.

findings.claim: A nonzero O(x3) lattice vector is counted as an admissible point with x4!=0 and gcd(x1,x2,x4)=1.
findings.decisive_evidence: Lambda_q=< (q^2,0),(0,1) >. For every fixed c and q>c, every vector of max norm <=cq has x1=0, so C=0 and x4=0. For prime q>2c all three root lattices have the same excluded-line obstruction. Exact illustration q=101,c=10 retained.
findings.impact: The claimed lower-bound proof for Theorem 1.4 counts inadmissible vectors. The main elliptic-family lower bound has a separate Lemma 5.8 argument and is not refuted.
findings.repair_limit: Need a new construction with nonzero C, required coprimality, and multiplicity control.

independent_verification.original_claim: Lemma 3.6 treats every nonzero Minkowski short vector as an admissible cubic-surface point.
independent_verification.assumptions: Same separable cubic, odd q=x3 coprime to discriminant 4, fixed short-vector constant c.
independent_verification.independent_proof: For alpha=0 modulo q^2 the lattice is <(q^2,0),(0,1)>. If q>c and max(|x1|,|x2|)<=cq then x1=0, so C=0 and x4=0, excluded. For prime q>2c, all three roots alpha=0,+1,-1 give q^2|(x1-alpha*x2) with absolute value <q^2, hence C=0. The exact q=101,c=10 enumeration corroborates, but the inequalities prove the unbounded obstruction.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Minkowski's nonzero vectors exist. Failure of this construction does not refute the global lower estimate or an alternative construction.
independent_verification.impact: The proof lacks admissible nonzero-C points and the required coprimality/multiplicity control.
independent_verification.repair: Construct and count points satisfying all admissibility conditions.
independent_verification.repair_limits: No replacement obtained. The main elliptic-family lower estimate uses separate Lemma 5.8 and is not refuted.

findings.location: PDF pp.33-35, definition L=K(sqrt(alpha)), Artin symbols, Lemma 8.4 application of Theorem 6.1
findings.claim: Specified L/Q and K21(sqrt(alpha21))/Q are Galois and contain K(sqrt(B)).
findings.decisive_evidence: K=Q(sqrt2), alpha=sqrt2, L=Q(2^(1/4)) subset R; T^4-2 Eisenstein and imaginary conjugates absent. sqrt(-2) is not in L. The invoked Galois hypothesis fails.
findings.impact: Undefined relative Galois group and invalid stated character-sum instantiation in the partial-torsion density argument.
findings.repair_limit: Use Kprime=K(sqrt B), Lprime=Kprime(sqrt alpha), redefine prime support and character parameters, then verify discriminants and all theorem conditions. Full revised proof not completed here.

independent_verification.original_claim: Section 8's field L and actual Theorem 6.1 invocation are Galois as required and contain K(sqrt B).
evidence_locations: Main pp.31-35 model, fields and invocation
independent_verification.assumptions: A=0,B=-2 gives nonsquare A^2-4B=8; delta=gamma1=gamma2=Dtilde=1 satisfies fixed-parameter requirements and R21=1.
independent_verification.independent_proof: K=Q(sqrt2), alpha=sqrt2, L=Q(2^(1/4)). T^4-2 is Eisenstein at 2. Its real-root degree-four field omits the imaginary conjugates, hence is not Galois. It also omits sqrt(-2), so Gal(L/K(sqrt B)) is undefined. R21=1 makes the actual K21(sqrt(alpha21)) equal this non-Galois L.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Restricting primes to split in K(sqrt B) can make the residue symbol independent of a prime choice, but does not fix the specified field or theorem hypothesis.
independent_verification.impact: Invalid stated Artin-group setup and character-sum invocation, including an intended unconditional subcase.
independent_verification.repair: Use K'=K(sqrt B), L'=K'(sqrt alpha). Since alpha*alphabar=B, the latter contains both conjugate square roots. Rebuild prime support and check degree, discriminant and all theorem parameters.
independent_verification.repair_limits: Full revised character-sum proof and uniform bounds were not completed. No density counterexample asserted.

findings.location: PDF pp.4-6, Theorem 2.5 range and proof of Theorem 2.4
findings.claim: m=O(logloglog N) suffices for the strict fixed-multiplier range m<Cprime logloglog N when k<=logloglog N and q=1/epsilon.
findings.decisive_evidence: m=ak/epsilon>=aL/(2epsilon)>=2Cprime L>Cprime L. Primary Smith Theorem 1.1 retains a fixed multiplier.
findings.impact: Uniform endpoint moments in Theorem 2.4 and their stated application are not justified by this invocation. No counterexample to the conclusion is asserted.
findings.repair_limit: The argument applies on a sufficiently smaller epsilon-dependent multiple of logloglog N, with a valid moment-input normalization. Recovering coefficient one needs stronger input or a new argument.

independent_verification.original_claim: An O(logloglog N) exponent may be used under the strict fixed coefficient in Theorem 2.5 for the full claimed moment range.
evidence_locations: Smith arXiv v2 pp.1-3, Theorem 1.1 p.2
independent_verification.assumptions: a=sigma log c>0,Cprime>0 fixed, L=logloglog N>=2, epsilon=min(1/2,a/(4Cprime)), k=floor(L), q=1/epsilon>1.
independent_verification.independent_proof: floor(L)>=L/2 gives m=ak/epsilon>=aL/(2epsilon)>=2Cprime L. If epsilon=1/2 then a>=2Cprime; otherwise the last coefficient equals 2Cprime. Thus m exceeds the required Cprime L for allowed endpoint k. The actual Smith statement retains a fixed coefficient too.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Increasing N cannot cure an excessive fixed multiplier. Failure of the invocation is not a counterexample to the moment theorem.
independent_verification.impact: Uniform endpoint moments and the stated application are not justified by this proof. Earlier density estimates do not depend on this later step.
independent_verification.repair: With a correctly normalized input, restrict k to e.g. Cprime*epsilon*L/(2a), or obtain a stronger input.
independent_verification.repair_limits: Coefficient-one range for every prescribed loss remains unproved; P6 is separate.

findings.location: PDF p.4, Theorem 2.5 universal m>0 normalization
findings.claim: The moment is <=exp(C m^2) for every sufficiently small positive m.

hypotheses_verified.rank_at_least_one: Nagell-Lutz integral torsion coordinates and nonintegral double

findings.decisive_evidence: For fixed large N, M=#D(N), mean>=1+(exp(m)-1)/M. Derivative at m=0 is 1/M>0, while exp(C m^2) has derivative 0. All sufficiently small positive m satisfy the upper-range condition and violate the bound.
findings.impact: Small-m formulation is false; the later intended m is bounded away from zero. Separate from P5.
findings.repair_limit: An explicit lower m restriction, fixed prefactor, or C(m+m^2) exponent avoids this obstruction; full corrected input must be supplied.

independent_verification.original_claim: The exponential-rank mean is <=exp(Cm^2) for all small positive m.
independent_verification.assumptions: E:y^2=x^3-2 is nonsingular and irreducible; D=1 belongs to D(N), with N fixed sufficiently large.
independent_verification.independent_proof: P=(3,5); exact doubling gives (129/100,-383/1000). By the standard Nagell-Lutz integral-coordinate criterion P cannot be torsion, so rank>=1. If M=#D(N), the mean is >=1+(exp(m)-1)/M. The derivative at zero of this lower bound minus exp(Cm^2) is 1/M>0. Every sufficiently small positive m violates the asserted bound while satisfying its upper-range condition.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The intended application has m bounded away from zero. This does not invalidate all larger-m information.
independent_verification.repair: A suitable fixed prefactor, exponent C(m+m^2), or lower restriction on m removes this obstruction.
independent_verification.repair_limits: A valid corrected input still must be supplied; P5 remains.

findings.impact: Displayed parameter choice does not give claimed saving, but a permitted alternative restores this step.
findings.repair_limit: Replace 5/8 by 3/8; field issue P4 still needs repair.

independent_verification.assumptions: Prior estimate allows any fixed positive epsilon.
independent_verification.counterevidence: A permitted replacement restores this local saving.

findings.location: PDF p.37, Section 8.2 short Weierstrass display after X=9x+3AD,Y=27y
findings.claim: The printed equation omits D^2,D^3 and uses old x.
findings.decisive_evidence: X=-15,Y=27. Printed RHS=-5157 (literal x) or -837 (X); Y^2=729. Correct RHS X^3+27(3B-A^2)D^2 X+27A(2A^2-9B)D^3=729. General identity checked symbolically.
findings.impact: Local model display false; corrected fixed-coefficient twist model and gcd bound prove the intended reduction.
findings.repair_limit: Insert the displayed corrected expression; this does not repair other estimates.

independent_verification.original_claim: The displayed short Weierstrass equation after X=9x+3AD,Y=27y is correct.
independent_verification.assumptions: Starting y^2=x(x^2+ADx+BD^2); A=-4,B=2,D=2,x=y=1 is an allowed point with nonsquare discriminant 8.
independent_verification.independent_proof: Symbolic expansion gives Y^2=X^3+27(3B-A^2)D^2 X+27A(2A^2-9B)D^3. The polynomial difference from 729x(x^2+ADx+BD^2) is zero. At X=-15,Y=27, corrected RHS=729; printed RHS=-5157 with literal x or -837 with X. Also gcd(X,D)=gcd(9x,D)|9gcd(x,D).
independent_verification.counterevidence: The corrected coefficients are fixed multiples of D^2,D^3 and recover the intended reduction.
independent_verification.impact: False local model display, explicitly repairable.
independent_verification.repair: Insert both twist powers and use X in the linear term.
independent_verification.repair_limits: Does not fix earlier counting or field estimates.
